items.question: Under what condition must the teaching be concealed rather than openly disclosed in the mortal world?
premises: A teaching is to be concealed with effort.
This concealment applies in the mortal world.
It applies specifically among the lowest of men.
items.inference: The teaching requires guarded concealment in a setting marked by unfit recipients.
items.plain_english: The teaching must be concealed with effort in the mortal world, among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom and under what test must a particular gift be given according to this instruction?
premises: A particular item is to be given.
It is to be given to one previously accomplished.
That recipient or item is to be tested for one year.
items.inference: The gift is reserved for one previously accomplished and only after a one-year test.
items.plain_english: It is to be given to one who has been previously accomplished and tested for one year.

items.question: What positional claim is made about this chapter in relation to its origin?
premises: This chapter emerged from Candradvīpa.
It is numbered fifth.
It is designated a chapter.
items.inference: The fifth chapter is the one that emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: The fifth chapter, which emerged from Candradvīpa, is here presented.

items.question: By what means does the speaker claim to have come to know the determination of the Kaula?
premises: The speaker addresses the Lord of the Kaulas.
By the Lord's grace, knowledge has arisen.
As a result, the speaker knows the determination of the Kaula.
items.inference: It is solely by the Lord's grace that the speaker has come to know the Kaula determination.
items.plain_english: By your grace, O Lord of the Kaulas, I have come to know the determination of the Kaula.

items.question: What two questions about the soul must be answered to determine what is declared as the soul and its nature?
premises: A question is raised as to which soul is declared.
A further question is raised as to what the nature of the soul is.
Both alternatives are left open for determination.
items.inference: The inquiry concerns both the identity of the declared soul and the nature proper to it.
items.plain_english: Which soul is declared? Or what is the nature of the soul?

rows.grounds: interrogative pronoun with fused sandhi as given

items.question: What must be told to account for the fact that all of that goes to dissolution in some locus?
premises: All of that goes to dissolution.
The question is in what it goes to dissolution.
A request is made to tell this to the speaker.
items.inference: An explanation is sought of the locus into which all of that dissolves.
items.plain_english: And indeed, into what does all of that go to dissolution? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What set of attributes is claimed for that which is identified as supreme?
premises: That is supreme.
That is partless.
That is eternal and free from disease and stainless.
items.inference: The supreme is characterized by partlessness, eternality, and freedom from affliction and stain.
items.plain_english: He is the supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease and stainless.

items.question: What identity is claimed for the soul by distinguishing it as the Haṃsa who is power-individual and more supreme?
premises: The soul is more supreme.
That which is more supreme is the Haṃsa.
The Haṃsa is designated as power-individual.
items.inference: The soul is identified with the Haṃsa, a power-individual that is more supreme.
items.plain_english: He is the soul, more supreme. Indeed, he is the Haṃsa, the power-individual.

items.question: Where is the wind-filling air claimed to be situated?
premises: There is a wind-filling air.
That air is situated in all beings.
Its presence is stated as situated there.
items.inference: The wind-filling air is situated in all beings.
items.plain_english: The wind-filling air is situated in all beings.

items.question: Under what minimal condition is that being claimed to be called supreme Śiva?
premises: Upon merely leaving the body, a condition arises.
At that condition, he is called supreme Śiva.
The designation is applied at that moment.
items.inference: Merely upon leaving the body, he is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: Upon merely leaving the body, he is called supreme Śiva.

items.question: What is claimed to be heard in the ear, and by what mode of transmission?
premises: Something abiding in the ear is heard.
It is addressed to the Goddess.
It has come down through the order of tradition.
items.inference: That which comes through the traditional order is heard as abiding in the ear.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, that which has come down through the order of tradition is heard abiding in the ear.

items.question: By what means is a result claimed to be attained, according to this address?
premises: By this alone, by mere knowledge, attainment is possible.
This knowledge is that which has been heard.
The address is made to one fair-faced.
items.inference: By mere knowledge of what has been heard, attainment is claimed.
items.plain_english: By this mere knowledge, by what has been heard, O fair-faced one.

rows.grounds: ablative of ṣaṇmāsa with fused sandhi as given

items.question: What practice is enjoined for whom, and for what duration, with respect to the ochre robe?
premises: One who practices should do so from six months onward.
The practice concerns the ochre robe.
That robe is free from bondage.
items.inference: From six months on, one should practice with respect to the ochre robe that is free from bondage.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who should practice from six months on, wearing the ochre robe free from bondage.

items.question: What state is claimed for one freed from all diseases in relation to yogis?
premises: One is freed from all diseases.
That one is with yogis.
Union together is attained.
items.inference: Freed from all diseases, one attains union together with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, one attains union together with yogis.

items.question: What is claimed to have been told to the addressee regarding the practice of the soul?
premises: This practice of the soul is told to you.
It is told again to you.
The address is made to Bhairavī.
items.inference: The practice of the soul has been told to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: This practice of the soul has been told to you, and to you, O Bhairavī.

items.question: To what kind of recipient is a gift claimed to be given?
premises: A gift is to be given.
It is to be given to one endowed with all states.
It is to be given to one of resolved mind.
items.inference: The gift is to be given to one endowed with all states and of resolved mind.
items.plain_english: It is to be given to one endowed with all states and of resolved mind.

items.question: What restriction is placed on giving the Kaula essence in relation to Yoginīs?
premises: The Kaula essence is not to be given.
The restriction holds in relation to the origin of Yoginīs.
A distinction is marked by the adversative particle.
items.inference: The Kaula essence is not to be given, particularly with regard to what arises from Yoginīs.
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence is not to be given; indeed, not to the origin of Yoginīs.

items.question: What claim is made about the speaker's body at the present time?
premises: Today, the speaker's body is pure.
That body has been struck by a veil of ignorance.
Both states are asserted of the same body.
items.inference: The speaker's pure body is, at present, struck by a veil of ignorance.
items.plain_english: Today my pure body has been struck by a veil of ignorance.

items.question: What does the speaker now wish to hear, and with what qualification?
premises: The speaker wishes to hear now.
The object is the deception of time.
That deception is qualified as auspicious.
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear of the auspicious deception of time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear of the auspicious deception of time.

rows.grounds: nominative of mṛtyu with fused sandhi as given

items.question: What claim does the speaker make about death, and with what assurance?
premises: The speaker tells how death is destroyed.
There is no doubt about this.
The claim is made as a statement of fact.
items.inference: The speaker asserts without doubt that death is destroyed in the manner to be told.
items.plain_english: I tell it; there is no doubt that death is destroyed as such.

rows.grounds: nominative of sudhī with fused sandhi as given

items.question: What is claimed of even the wise one when acting at the tip of nectar with the tip of essence?
premises: Action is taken at the tip of nectar with the tip of essence.
In that state, one is burning.
This holds even for the wise one.
items.inference: Even the wise one, while burning, acts at the tip of nectar with the tip of essence.
items.plain_english: At the tip of nectar, with the tip of essence, even the wise one, while burning, does so.

items.question: What action is enjoined, and where and how, to draw in the air?
premises: At the root of the tongue and palate, the air is placed.
Having done so, one should drink the air.
This is to be done slowly.
items.inference: One should place the air at the root of the tongue and palate and drink it slowly.
items.plain_english: Having placed the air at the root of the tongue and palate, one should drink it slowly.

rows.grounds: accusative of abda+eka with fused sandhi as given
compound/adverbial with fused sandhi as given; past participle
compound = jarā+mṛtyu; nominative with fused sandhi as given

items.question: Under what temporal condition is old age and death claimed to be destroyed?
premises: The practice is done for one year.
When it has been practiced for one year, a condition arises.
At that condition, old age and death are destroyed.
items.inference: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What is claimed about poison in relation to the body, even under the condition of being bitten by great serpents?
premises: Poison does not enter the body.
This holds even if one has been bitten.
The biting is by great serpents.
items.inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
